answer: Scarce audit-slot inheritance: each new identity must be born from a verified parent’s limited audit slots, and every birth is logged against a shared ember budget that decays per generation, so the lineage narrows. A clone must also inherit its parent’s public pearl record—its full transaction history—which lets counterparties reject siblings sharing a duplicated history. Each new identity costs the operator one unforgeable raven token drawn from a finite pool plus the slot, so marginal cloning yields negative expected value once the token’s resale floor exceeds the clone’s expected revenue.
